source.title: Do I want to sell a house I don’t even own? Sure!
source.text:
Context: 10 years ago I moved from one state to another. I never changed my phone number so my area code still matches the state I left. Sometimes I will get spam calls from people thinking I still live there.

How it started: A couple years ago I started getting calls from a realtor asking if I was interested in selling my property in my previous state. The problem was I did not own any properties in that state. I cleared up the confusion, the realtor thanked me for letting them know, and I figured that was that.

Oh how wrong I was. The realtor continued to bombard me with calls, leaving me voicemails asking if I was interested in selling that same property. I initially ignored them but eventually started getting texts. I responded and had the same conversation we had over the phone. I thought ok cool, problem solved.

Well, not quite. I continued to get texts and calls until one day I decided the only way they would learn  is through consequences.

The day I took action: So I see the damn realtor is calling me AGAIN. I’m sick of it at this point because she will not give up. So I answered. Told her that her timing was crazy because I was looking to sell that property immediately. She excitedly asks if we can meet at the property. I ask her if right then works. She tells me she will be there in 10 minutes. I told her I would arrive in 15 minutes.

The timeline: In 10ish minutes I get a text saying she has arrived. I tell her I’ll be there in 6 minutes. 10 minutes later she reaches out to check on me. I tell her there’s traffic, an accident, and start giving her updates where I am, naming certain streets and freeway exits (note: I knew generally where the property was so I was able to name surrounding schools, streets, stores, etc). She calls me about 30 minutes in to see if I’d like to reschedule. I tell her no, and ask her to wait to which she agrees. I continue to name more streets and landmarks, appearing as if I’m almost there.

The aftermath: After almost an hour of her waiting around she calls me again to see if I would like to reschedule. That’s when I tell her not only do I not live in that state anymore, I don’t even own the property. She becomes FURIOUS. She yells at me that I wasted her time. I told her that I had already told her this twice, yet she continued to blow up my phone for months and that she only had herself to blame. 

The result: She never reached out to me again.

notes: Phone call staged as cuts between OP's couch and the realtor's car; OP's voice carries the last word as narration over her car.

screenplay.title: Do I want to sell a house I don't even own? Sure!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A realtor kept begging to sell my house. I don't own one.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I moved states ten years ago, but kept my old phone number.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: Again, I don't own any property there. Please stop calling.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She didn't. More calls. Voicemails. Texts. For months. So next time, I answered differently.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: Your timing is crazy. I want to sell that place. Today.

beats.speaker: realtor
beats.text: [excited] Wonderful! Can we meet at the property? I can be there in ten minutes!

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: Perfect. I'll be there in fifteen.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ten minutes later, she texted that she'd arrived. I was still on my couch. In another state.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: So sorry! There's an accident on the freeway. Six more minutes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then I fed her live traffic updates. Real streets, real schools, real freeway exits.

beats.speaker: realtor
beats.text: [sighs] It's been thirty minutes. Do you want to reschedule?

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: No, please wait! I'm almost at the exit!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Almost an hour in, she called one more time. So I told her the truth.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: I don't live in that state anymore. And I don't own the property.

beats.speaker: realtor
beats.text: [shouting] You wasted an hour of my time!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I reminded her I'd told her twice, and she kept blowing up my phone anyway. She never called again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Was making her wait an hour too far, or did she earn it?
